claims.text: The alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
WTaTiVZr is composed of reduced-activation refractory elements suitable for easier post-service recycling in nuclear applications.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature loading.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr creates heterogeneous local stress fields.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr promotes the nucleation and stability of nano-twins.
High-temperature deformation of WTaTiVZr promotes dynamic recovery features, including refined dislocation substructures and subgrains.
Plastic deformation of TaTiVWZr is dislocation dominated, and increasing temperature thermally activates dislocation motion.
Nano-twins can provide barriers to dislocation motion while also providing pathways for dislocation slip.
A hierarchical twin network can produce simultaneous strength, ductility, strain hardening, and high fracture toughness.
Nano-twins act as additional slip systems in WTaTiVZr.
Nano-twinning and dynamic recovery delay dislocation pile-up and crack initiation in WTaTiVZr.
Pure tungsten deforms more brittly than WTaTiVZr under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
The relevant plasma-facing-component operational temperature range is approximately 600–1000 °C.
Nano-twinning and thermally activated dynamic recovery are effective in WTaTiVZr throughout 600–1000 °C.
Under identical high-temperature TEM straining, WTaTiVZr will show a higher nano-twin density and more refined, dynamic dislocation structures than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature TEM straining, WTaTiVZr will show delayed crack initiation relative to pure tungsten.
The comparison will use recrystallized polycrystalline WTaTiVZr and pure tungsten tested with identical temperature profiles, strain rates, environments, and similar specimen microstructures.
Failure to observe enhanced nano-twinning, dynamic recovery, delayed cracking, plastic strain, or toughness in WTaTiVZr relative to tungsten would falsify the hypothesis.
